topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss primary non-targeted treatment modalities, including surgical excision, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, alongside their associated toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and kinase inhibitor therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the concept of oncogene addiction, the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors, and the clinical challenges of drug resistance, bypass pathways, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine antibody-targeted therapeutics, including naked monoclonal antibodies targeting cell surface receptors and antibody-drug conjugates designed to deliver cytotoxic agents selectively to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the evidence for immune surveillance against tumors and the major immunotherapeutic strategies used to re-engage the immune system, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR-T cell therapy.

topics.label: Current challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate overall progress in cancer management, genomic profiling, survival trends across cancer types, and future clinical and ethical dilemmas in treatment.
